messages:
Iris: Following the RFC review, proposal: introduce a small 'stabilizer' control plane that centralizes automatic rollback/fallback decisions. Router stays simple and resilient: it takes a best-effort hint from stabilizer but must have a deterministic local fallback. High-level tradeoffs?

Nikhil: OK with separation. Biggest risk is introducing a dependency on the hot path. We need strict budgets: routers should never block more than ~4ms waiting for a hint for common requests.

Sam: where do signals come from? stabilizer needs low-latency probes (mirror + synthetic) and aggregated metrics for smoothing. suggest event-driven probe ingestion + periodic tsdb pulls.

Iris: agreed. quick sketch: probes -> pubsub -> stabilizer (streamed). stabilizer writes decisions and audit events to kafka. routers subscribe to policy streams and keep local cache; routers call a fast Hint RPC with 3ms timeout when they want a live opinion.

Priya: decision semantics: rule-first, ML as advisor. outputs should be compact enums + reason codes: e.g., ACTION=HOLD/ROLLBACK/ALLOW, REASON=[lat_p95,err_spike]. Avoid black-box rollbacks.

Nikhil: proto idea: 
```proto
service Stabilizer {
  rpc Hint(HintRequest) returns (HintReply) {} // low-latency; optional
  rpc PolicyStream(stream SubReq) returns (stream Policy) {}
}
```
HintReply minimal fields: {action, target_variant, reason_codes, nonce, expiry_ms}. Router validates expiry and nonce to be replay-safe.

Sam: about state: recommend stabilizer be authoritative for cohort assignment (so sampling and probe cohorts are consistent), but not authoritative for session affinity. routers keep session TTL locally. stabilizer can issue signed revocations to force immediate switches when necessary.

Priya: revocation token pattern: short-lived HMAC token with version and decision_id. router validates HMAC locally; no extra network calls required. Good compromise.

Rory: ops ask: tenants want visibility and manual override. we must emit an audit stream with compact events: {t, tenant, from, to, reasons, decision_id, initiator}. expose last N decisions in UI and provide manual rollback button (which creates an explicit decision event).

Iris: monitoring metrics stabilizer should emit: decision.latency_ms, decision.count, signal_ingest_lag_ms, rollback.count, revoke.count. correlate by tenant/model. Also emit probe success/failure rates.

Nikhil: invariants to codify: 1) routers may not switch unless TTL expired or stabilizer action received. 2) stabilizer actions are idempotent and include versioning & nonces. 3) router deterministic tie-breaker if stabilizer unreachable.

Sam: policy DSL minimal example (YAML-like):
```
policies:
  - id: conservative-1
    cohorts:
      - name: probe-1
        pct: 0.5
      - name: pilot-1
        pct: 2
    signals:
      - p50_lat > 150
      - error_rate > 1%
    actions:
      - on: error_rate > 2%
        do: ROLLBACK
```
Keep it small so humans can reason and ops can tweak safely.

Priya: chaos plan: simulate stabilizer full outage, high-latency hints, and noisy signals. Verify routers stay on safe defaults and do not oscillate. Also test signed revocation replay protections.

ops-bot: scheduled test: stabilizer-latency-injection -> 2026-01-10T03:00:00Z

Rory: one more product note: allow per-tenant opt-outs and a manual-exempt flag. enterprise tenants will want to pin behavior. Also surface safety presets: conservative/default/aggressive.

Iris: next steps I propose:
1) short RFC with proto, DSL, failure modes, and invariants (~600 words)
2) implement a mock stabilizer + router Hint hook behind a feature flag
3) run chaos scenarios and add monitoring/runbook updates

Nikhil: I'll own the mock + perf budget tests.

Sam: I'll own telemetry ingestion and probe wiring.

Priya: I'll draft the decision schema, revocation token format, and safety thresholds.

Rory: product will draft tenant UI and override flow.

Iris: I'll open the RFC tomorrow and tag owners. thanks all! :tada:
